claims.text: Menopause is diagnosed clinically: no menses for 12 months with no other likely cause.
claims.quote: Diagnosis of menopause is clinical; it is confirmed retroactively when a woman has had no menses for 12 months and there is no other suspected cause.

claims.text: Consider other causes: pregnancy, other causes of amenorrhea, and uterine cancer causing abnormal bleeding.
claims.quote: However, pregnancy, amenorrhea due to other etiologies, or abnormal uterine bleeding due to uterine cancer should be considered.

claims.text: Prolonged amenorrhea under age 40: suspect primary ovarian insufficiency.
claims.quote: Primary ovarian insufficiency should be suspected in women with prolonged amenorrhea at < 40 years old.

claims.text: FSH is rarely needed (eg, after hysterectomy or at a younger age); one value can mislead, and consistently high levels confirm menopause.
claims.quote: FSH levels may be measured, but this test is rarely necessary except perhaps in women who have had a hysterectomy and in women who are younger than the usual age of menopause. A single measurement may not be informative, because levels fluctuate during the menopausal transition. Consistently elevated levels confirm menopause.
